land.text: Lagash, Girsu and Nina, tributary to Uruk (En-hegal) and to Mesilim of Kish (Lugal-sha-engur) before Ur-Nanshe 'achieved independence, making himself king'

predecessors.note: The collective sumerian-city-states books the same ground as a split (-2520) and gets it back as a gain at the dissolve (-2340) since the me-01 fix; the city is drawn over the collective.

land.text: Lugal-zage-si of Umma 'annexed most of the territory of Lagash under king Urukagina'; his Uruk-based kingdom is the collective's last phase

capitals.name: Girsu (Tello)
capitals.note: 'Girsu (modern Telloh), about 25 km (16 mi) northwest of Lagash' was the religious center; the state is named for Lagash (Al-Hiba, 46.41 E 31.41 N, Dhi Qar Governorate), and Nina (Tell Zurghul) 'marks the southern limit of the state'. Girsu is not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: 'the Lagash state incorporated the cities of Lagash, Girsu, and Nina'; Girsu 25 km north-west, Nina 'around 10 km (6.2 mi) away, marks the southern limit of the state'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Lagash polity. Ur-Nanshe 'r. c. 2520 BC', Akurgal 'r. c. 2500 BC (MC) (9 years)'.

correction.text: Eannatum's hegemony: he 'conquered all of Sumer, including Ur, Nippur, Akshak (controlled by Zuzu), Larsa, and Uruk', made Umma a tributary and 'demanded tribute as far as Mari'. Drawn as Sumer without Umma (30 km, vassal tint) and Ur (40 km, hatched occupation), which keep their own keyframes; Susa is not drawn here but hatched on elam's side (the Susa occupation of the ledger)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for Eannatum (fl. c. 2450). Mari and Umma are vassal tint, Susa and Ur hatched (ledger). The Stele of the Vultures 'was set up c. 2450 BCE'. [fixer me-01: the first version was 'Sumer plus Susa 60 km', which drew Susa as territory and double-claimed Umma and Ur.]

correction.text: Lagash, Girsu, Nina and the Gu-edena after Eannatum: Kish 'regained its independence after his death'; Entemena 'increased the power of Lagash during his rule'; Urukagina (r. c. 2350, 11 years) was 'defeated by Lugalzagesi'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Enannatum I (c. 2425), Entemena, Enannatum II, Enentarzi, Lugalanda (all 'c. 2400' on the page), Urukagina (c. 2350): the pages give no further border for the city-state; the Gu-edena stayed contested with Umma to c. 2400.

ledger.note: 2520 BCE: Ur-Nanshe makes himself king of Lagash. 'Ur-Nanshe ... r. c. 2520 BC'; the History of Sumer page: he 'achieved independence, making himself king', defeated Ur and 'captured the king of Umma, Pabilgaltuk'; before him En-hegal 'was tributary to Uruk' and Lugal-sha-engur 'to Mesilim of Kish'.

region.text: 'the Guʾedena, a fertile area lying between them'

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: Lagash and Umma fall out over the Gu-edena. 'In c. 2450 BC, Lagash and the neighboring city of Umma fell out with each other after a border dispute over the Guʾedena'; the Stele of the Vultures 'commemorates the victory of Eannatum of Lagash over Ush, king of Umma' and Eannatum 'made a boundary treaty with Ush's successor, Enakalle' (r. c. 2445).

region.text: 'all of Sumer, including Ur, Nippur, Akshak (controlled by Zuzu), Larsa, and Uruk': Sumer apart from Umma and Ur

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: Eannatum masters Sumer. 'conquered all of Sumer'; 'He defeated Kish, Akshak, and Mari from the Antasurra of Ningirsu'; he 'claimed the title of King of Kish' and his domain extended 'over the rest of Sumer and Akkad'. The counterpart is Ur, whose hegemony over Sumer Eannatum ended (first-dynasty-of-ur loss -2450; 'defeated Umma, defeated Ur') [reviewer me-01: counterpart changed from sumerian-city-states].
2450 BCE: Umma pays tribute to Lagash after Ush's defeat and the treaty with Enakalle. The History of Sumer page: 'Umma became tributary under Eannatum'.

region.text: Mari, from which he 'demanded tribute as far as Mari'

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: Mari pays tribute to Lagash. The Early Dynastic page: Eannatum 'was able to defeat Mari and Elam around 2450 B.C.'.

region.text: Elam: 'the city Az off the coast of the modern Persian Gulf' and 'the city of Susa'

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: Eannatum overruns Elam. 'He conquered parts of Elam, including the city Az' and destroyed 'the city of Susa'; the Awan page dates the defeat 'c. 2450 BC'. Hatched; no page says Lagash administered Susa.

2450 BCE: Eannatum holds Ur. He 'conquered all of Sumer, including Ur, Nippur, Akshak (controlled by Zuzu), Larsa, and Uruk'. Hatched; the city stays drawn from first-dynasty-of-ur_-2450 (mirror there).

region.text: Kish: 'He defeated Kish, Akshak, and Mari from the Antasurra of Ningirsu'

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: Eannatum takes Kish. 'He defeated Kish, Akshak, and Mari from the Antasurra of Ningirsu' and he 'claimed the title of "King of Kish" (which regained its independence after his death)'. Hatched; mirror of kish /ledger/2.

region.text: the rest of Sumer: Sumer apart from Umma and Ur

ledger.note: 2425 BCE: Eannatum's hegemony lapses at his death. Enannatum I 'r. c. 2425 BC (MC) (4 years)'; Kish 'regained its independence after his death' and 'revolts often arose in parts of his empire' (Eannatum page). Year bridged to the successor's accession.
2425 BCE: Umma throws off the tribute. Ur-Lumma 'r. c. 2425 BC' (Umma page); the History of Sumer page: Ur-Lumma 'attacked Lagash unsuccessfully'. Year bridged.
2425 BCE: Mari's tribute ends with Eannatum. Bridged; no page dates it.
2425 BCE: Lagash leaves Elam. Bridged to Enannatum I's accession.
2425 BCE: the hold on Ur lapses at Eannatum's death (Enannatum I 'r. c. 2425 BC'; 'revolts often arose in parts of his empire'). Bridged.

2400 BCE: Entemena settles the Umma frontier (the end is bridged: the pages date only Entemena's report, not a settlement; reviewer me-01 lowered confidence from 2). The conflict is 'reported c. 2400 BC by Entemena'; Il of Umma 'r. c. 2420 BC', 'temp. of Entemena'; the History of Sumer page: 'Entemena subdued Illi with an ally, Lugal-kinishe-dudu' of Uruk. Giššakidu (c. 2400) follows at Umma.

2400 BCE: Kish is independent again. Kug-Bau (r. c. 2400 BC) 'said to have gained independence from En-anna-tum I of Lagash and En-shag-kush-ana of Uruk' (historicity uncertain); the Eannatum page puts the lapse at his death (c. 2425). Year follows the Kish page and the kish dossier (/ledger/3).

region.text: 'most of the territory of Lagash under king Urukagina'

ledger.note: 2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si of Umma conquers Lagash. He 'annexed most of the territory of Lagash under king Urukagina'; the Lagash page: Urukagina 'r. c. 2350 BC (MC) (11 years)' was 'defeated by Lugalzagesi, beginning when Lugalzagesi was ruler of Umma and culminating as ruler of Uruk'. Lugal-zage-si's kingdom (r. c. 2358–2334 or c. 2340–2316) is the collective's last phase; Lagash under Akkadian governors follows from c. 2300.

wars.name: Lagash–Umma border conflict

zones.text: 'the Guʾedena, a fertile area lying between them'

wars.outcome: Eannatum defeated Ush (Stele of the Vultures), made Umma tributary and fixed the boundary with Enakalle; Ur-Lumma and Il of Umma renewed the war; Entemena, with Lugal-kinishe-dudu of Uruk, subdued Il and 'reported' the conflict c. 2400.
wars.note: Mesilim of Kish (r. c. 2550 on the Kish page, 'c. 2500 BC' on the Early Dynastic page) 'acted as arbitrator in a Lagash–Umma conflict' earlier. Gu-edena is not in the gazetteer.

wars.name: Eannatum's campaigns
wars.outcome: 'conquered all of Sumer', repulsed Akshak, 'defeated Kish, Akshak, and Mari', 'allegedly smote Shubur', conquered parts of Elam; Kish 'regained its independence after his death'.

wars.name: Lugal-zage-si's conquest of Lagash
wars.outcome: Urukagina defeated; Lagash's territory 'annexed' by Lugal-zage-si.

certainty.note: The Gu-edena border with Umma is the one dated line (Mesilim's arbitration, Eannatum's 'boundary treaty' with Enakalle, Entemena's report); everything else is a city territory with soft edges.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks: the First Dynasty of Lagash, -2520 (Ur-Nanshe) to -2340 (Urukagina's defeat by Lugal-zage-si), with Eannatum's short hegemony over Sumer (-2450..-2425) as a new keyframe. The overlap with the collective sumerian-city-states is booked on both sides since the me-01 fix (split -2520, Sumer lost -2425 as the collective's gain, dissolve -2340 as its gain); the city is drawn over the collective's shapes. Eannatum's K1 is Sumer without Umma and Ur (vassal tint and hatched occupation in the ledger) and without Susa (hatched; the Susa occupation is lagash's, with elam as counterpart); Kish is a hatched occupation -2450..-2400 (mirror of kish). Lagash under Akkadian governors (c. 2300–2164) is Akkadian territory; the Second Dynasty (Ur-Baba, Gudea) is second-dynasty-of-lagash. Ruler dates on the Lagash page are round ('c. 2400' for four rulers) so no ruler strip is given. Umma, Girsu, Nina and the Gu-edena are not in the gazetteer; Lagash, Susa, Mari, Kish are.

THIN ITEMS (me-01 fixer): the Enannatum I page (opened) says only that Umma under Ur-Lumma 'once more asserted independence' and attacked Lagash unsuccessfully, and nothing about Eannatum's empire or its end; the Entemena page (opened) dates his war with Il of Umma only by 'c. 2400 BC', says it was won 'through an alliance with Lugal-kinishe-dudu of Uruk', and mentions neither the Gu-edena nor tribute from Umma or Mari. The end of the hegemony (-2425), the vassal ends and the contest end (-2400) therefore stay bridged at confidence 1.
